title: Prefix probing harness and staged TTL applier for safe cost tuning
creator: Leah Martinez
description: Build a lightweight probing harness that samples prefix populations across traffic slices to estimate realistic hit-rate curves, then use those estimates to drive a staged TTL applier (staged-config) that safely reduces cache TTLs to lower token cost while bounding latency regressions. This ticket covers the experiment harness, a deterministic probe scheduler, TTL recommendation heuristics, and an automated staged apply/rollback controller that integrates with our rollout engine.
acceptance_criteria: Probing harness deployed to canary with <5% extra tail latency under probe load
Hit-rate model produces stable recommendations for TTL reductions with documented confidence bands
Staged TTL applier can apply to 1%, 10%, 50%, and 100% cohorts with automated rollback on defined SLO violations
End-to-end test coverage for probe scheduler, model pipeline, and rollback triggers
Runbook updated and linked; SRE sign-off obtained
implementation_notes: Probe method: deterministic sampling using hashed request key mod N to avoid user bias; probes should be cheap reads to shadow-store to compute miss/hit without affecting live cache state
Model: lightweight exponential-moving-average + Bayesian shrinkage per-prefix to produce hit-rate + CI. We will avoid heavy ML models for operational simplicity.
Recommendation heuristic: for each prefix produce TTL candidates and estimate cost delta + expected added tail latency; rank by cost-savings per-ppoint-of-latency
Staged applier: integrate with rollout service to enforce cohort gating and shadow canaries; include a dry-run mode that writes planned TTLs to annotations only
Safety gates: min TTL floors per prefix, max daily delta across global cache, and mandatory rollback on >0.5% increase in 99th percentile token latency for the affected routes
tests_and_rollout_plan: Unit tests for probe scheduler and model fitting logic
Integration test that runs probe harness against synthetic traffic generator (open-source traffic-sim) in CI
End-to-end smoke in staging: apply to 1% cohort for 24h, monitor cost and latency metrics, then 10% for 48h, then 50%/100% with step validations
Rollback triggers: metric thresholds and anomaly detector tie-ins; rollback automated via rollout service and human-notify channel
Dry-run window: first 48h must run in dry-run before any live TTL changes are applied for a given customer tier
monitoring_and_metrics: Per-prefix: probe hit-rate, probe sample count, estimated cost delta, recommended TTLs
Per-route: 50/95/99 latency, token throughput, cache miss rate
Global: daily cost savings estimate, number of rollbacks, number of automated applies
Alerts: anomalies in 99th latency, spike in miss rate >10% relative to baseline, sustained probe sample variance >20%
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: probes add measurable load and skew metrics. Mitigation: use low-rate deterministic sampling and shadow reads that are throttled per shard.

Risk: incorrect TTL suggestions reduce cache effectiveness for long-tail prefixes. Mitigation: conservative shrink factor and require CI > 0.7 for autonomous applies; otherwise surface to ops for review.

Risk: rollout engine bug causes widespread TTL churn. Mitigation: staged cohorts, canary first to non-critical tenants, and final 100% only after 72h and SLO pass. Manual stop button available in console.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Leah M: spike complete; probe harness shows stable sampling with 0.7% median added p50 latency in staging during low traffic windows. Uploaded initial telemetry samples to drive.
2025-02-13 - Ravi S: implemented deterministic sampler. Putting up PR for review (prototype PR link above). Need to confirm shard-level throttling values with SRE.
2025-02-14 - Nikhil (SRE): reviewed probe load; recommended reducing probe rate on hot shards and adding exponential backoff for retries. Also suggested adding probe-tag to traces.
2025-02-16 - PM review (Hana Ortiz): prefer conservative default: do not autoscale TTL < 60s for non-stable prefixes. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-18 - Engineering: integrated model outputs with rollout annotations. Built unit tests for CI. Started dry-run in staging for the 1% cohort.

2025-02-20 - Observability: early dry-run shows expected cost delta estimates but a small (0.2%) bump in 95th latency for two legacy routes. Deciding threshold for rollback: currently set to 0.5% — holding live applies until root cause investigated.

2025-02-22 - Decision: lower default shrink factor from 0.8 to 0.65 for automated applies and add mandatory human approval when predicted latency delta >0.25% for high-traffic routes. Ravi assigned to implement the approval flow.
